business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real Estate Property Management and Rental Screening Cloud

stage_1.document_name: Notarized copy of passport (identification) of each director and each beneficial owner/subscriber
stage_1.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the person's country of nationality / notary public in that country
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention states; consular legalization at the South African High Commission/Embassy for non-Convention states)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2022 — ss. 13 (incorporation), 14 (notice of incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal capacity), 31 (share capital/no par value), 66 (board of directors), 86 (company secretary) and Chapter 5 (fundamental transactions); Companies Regulations, 2011, including Regulation 14 (name objections) and Forms CoR 9.1, CoR 14.1 and CoR 44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a public entity under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic), operating the CIPC e-Services online registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) filed through the CIPC e-Services 'New Companies' workflow; optional prior name reservation on Form CoR 9.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory share capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the company must, however, allot at least one ordinary share upon incorporation, and the MOI may stipulate the authorised share classes. Issued share subscription proceeds must be credited to a South African corporate bank account in the company's name. For a foreign subscriber, the inward payment is subject to SARB Exchange Control Regulations administered through an Authorised Dealer (bank); funds exceeding the prescribed threshold require a blocked 'share consideration' escrow arrangement or prior SARB approval before shares are issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
[COMPANY] (PTY) LTD — FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

RESOLVED that: (1) the allotment of ordinary shares to the founding subscriber and receipt of share subscription monies into the company's designated South African bank account are ratified and recorded in the securities register; (2) the registered office at [street address] is adopted as the domicilium citandi et executandi for all statutory notices; (3) [Name A] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name B] Chief Financial Officer, with mandate limits and signing authority approved by the board; (4) a company secretary is waived under s.86(1) for this private company and record-keeping duties are delegated to the CFO; and (5) the directors are authorised to complete CIPC post-incorporation filings, SARS registration, COIDA registration and corporate bank account opening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and pre-incorporation search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services online portal (cipc.co.za) — Name Reservations module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search against the CIPC Companies and Trademarks register; select up to three preferred names in priority order; complete and lodge Form CoR 9.1 electronically; pay the statutory reservation fee by card or EFT. The reservation is valid for six months and may be transferred to the company upon incorporation. The name should avoid similarity to existing trademarks and must not be offensive or misleading under Regulation 14.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name(s) in priority sequence
Applicant's South African ID or foreign passport copy
Proof of residential address of the applicant
Completed CoR 9.1 form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or an objection is lodged under Regulation 14, file a fresh CoR 9.1 containing alternative names, or respond in writing to the Registrar's objection notice within 20 business days; a contested reservation may be referred to the Companies Tribunal for review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and subscriber execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors or a duly admitted legal practitioner; foreign subscribers require notarisation and apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention before lodgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) on the CIPC pre-approved template or as a bespoke MOI, setting out share classes, authorised shares, director appointment rules, and incorporation provisions. The founding subscriber(s) must sign before a commissioner of oaths; signatures executed outside South Africa must be notarised and apostilled. The subscriber must adopt the MOI in writing and confirm the registered office postal address and physical address.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A template or bespoke draft)
Subscriber signature pages or notarised powers of attorney
Written adoption resolution of the subscribers
FICA due-diligence pack for each subscriber (ID/passport and proof of address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI is rejected by CIPC as non-compliant with the Companies Act or Regulations, amend the MOI and file a correcting notice of amendment (CoR 15.1) or resubmit a fresh CoR 14.1 with the revised MOI within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — new company registration transaction via e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) in the CIPC e-Services 'New Companies' workflow; upload the executed MOI and director/subscriber details; pay the company registration fee of approximately ZAR 175. Upon approval, the system automatically issues the enterprise number, creates the CIPC company profile, and notifies SARS of the registration. Download the stamped CoR 14.1 and the Certificate of Incorporation as conclusive proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed CoR 14.1 with company name and registered office
Executed Memorandum of Incorporation (PDF)
Director and company secretary particulars and consents
Proof of payment of the CIPC registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete or queried, respond with corrections through the CIPC case management module within 20 business days; if the registration is voided for defective filing, lodge a fresh CoR 14.1 using the same name reservation reference at no additional name reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS income tax, VAT and employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Income Tax on SARS eFiling using the CIPC-issued enterprise number; complete ITREG to obtain an Income Tax reference number; if annual taxable turnover exceeds or is reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1 million, register for VAT (Form VAT101) and request a VAT clearance certificate. The company must also register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL once it appoints employees, using the combined employer registration form.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and stamped CoR 14.1
Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' ID documents and personal income tax numbers
Bank account confirmation letter
Projected turnover or financial estimates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration (e.g., duplicate ITREG or outdated business description), correct the submission online or through a SARS branch case; late registrations attract administrative penalties which may be waived where reasonable cause is demonstrated in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Compensation Fund, Department of Employment and Labour — e-Registration portal or provincial labour centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the employer registration form (W.As. 2) to the Compensation Fund together with the projected remuneration schedule and company profile. The Fund issues an assessment number and an annual letter of good standing which must be maintained for all employees. Pair this registration with the UIF employer declaration through the Department of Employment and Labour.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
SARS employer registration number
Completed W.As. 2 Employer Registration Form
Projected remuneration schedule of employees
Directors' ID copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employer registration is delayed or rejected, carry forward the CIPC certificate and SARS registration to the provincial Labour Centre or appeal in writing to the Compensation Fund Commissioner; retrospective registration with a late-payment waiver may be requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership disclosure and FIC compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership module; Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) if the company qualifies as an accountable institution under Schedule 1 of the FIC Act 38 of 2001
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the Beneficial Ownership declaration (CoR 44.1) with CIPC identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly owns or exercises control over the company's voting rights, shares, or effective control, in compliance with the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022. Confirm whether the entity must register with the FIC — a PropertyTech SaaS receiving tenant screening and payment data is generally not an accountable institution unless it performs estate agency or letting-agent functions involving the transfer of trust money.
required_dossiers: CoR 44.1 Beneficial Ownership form
Ownership structure diagrams or trust deeds for indirect holdings
ID or passport copies of all beneficial owners
FIC Risk and Compliance Return (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Non-filing or inaccurate beneficial ownership data is subject to CIPC administrative penalties; cure by filing an amended CoR 44.1 within five business days and paying the prescribed late fee; deliberate misstatements may be referred to the Companies Tribunal or the National Prosecuting Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of corporate bank account and share capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised Dealer / commercial bank (e.g., Standard Bank, ABSA, FNB or Nedbank) acting under the SARB Exchange Control Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the bank's FICA onboarding package; submit the Certificate of Incorporation and MOI; adopt a board resolution on banking mandate with dual-signatory limits; provide the beneficial ownership declaration. The bank keys in the share subscription proceeds to the corporate account. A foreign shareholder's inward payment exceeding the prescribed threshold must be routed through an authorised dealer and may require SARB approval or a blocked share-consideration arrangement before the shares are issued.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
First board resolution / banking mandate resolution
Director ID or passport and proof of residential address (FICA)
Lease agreement proving the physical business address
SARS tax clearance and VAT registration letter (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the mandate or requests further FATCA/CRS or FICA documentation, rectify by supplementing the onboarding pack or choosing an alternate authorised dealer; the company may open a blocked 'share consideration' account pending the correction of filings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (computer programming / cloud-based PropTech SaaS) is a non-industrial service activity and requires no operational licence from the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic). Should the entity later operate physical premises or an on-premise data centre, municipal business licensing under the Businesses Act 71 of 1991 would fall under the local municipality's Economic Development Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for cloud-based real-estate rental screening SaaS. The company must, however, maintain a valid Certificate of Occupancy or lease agreement for its registered office, and an IT services/SLA with data centres. POPIA registration with the Information Regulator is a separate mandatory data-protection registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE); local municipal environmental health department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — an office-based PropTech SaaS activity is not listed in Listing Notices 1–3 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 (as amended); no environmental authorisation is required unless the entity constructs a data centre or installs backup power generators exceeding the listed thresholds (e.g., ≥ 10 MW or ≥ 1 MVA backup generation may trigger a basic assessment).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC discharge applies to the SaaS classification. Ordinary office effluent must comply with municipal sewerage by-laws and the National Water Act 36 of 1998, s.21 provisions. Any backup diesel generator must meet the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 listed-activity thresholds and local noise/nuisance by-laws; e-waste must be disposed of through a registered recycler under the Extended Producer Responsibility regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local fire authority (e.g., Fire and Rescue Services of the relevant metropolitan municipality) confirming compliance with the National Building Regulations and SANS 10400; Electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC) for the leased office premises; Certificate of Occupancy or structural load clearance for the registered office; compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including a risk assessment, emergency evacuation plan, first-aid kit, and public indemnity insurance covering premises access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za, administered by SARS Head Office, Lehae La SARS, 299 Bronkhorst Street, Brooklyn, Pretoria
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African (Pty) Ltd is registered with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and receives a company registration number. SARS eFiling is then used to obtain the income tax reference number. VAT vendor registration is applied for via SARS form VAT 101. Compulsory VAT registration applies once taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed R1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration may be granted where taxable supplies exceed R50,000 in the preceding 12 months, subject to SARS conditions. Foreign-owned local (Pty) Ltd entities follow the standard resident company registration route. Foreign suppliers of electronic services to South African residents may be required to use the simplified SARS section 54 VAT registration route and to appoint a local representative taxpayer where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed as a separate taxpayer on its worldwide income. There is no pass-through treatment. Dividends tax is withheld at shareholder level; capital gains tax is imposed on the company's taxable capital gains; the branch income of a non-resident foreign company carrying on business in South Africa is taxed on a representative basis, but the domestic (Pty) Ltd is the planned entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election. Tax classification is determined by the Companies Act and Income Tax Act. Relevant elections include VAT group vendor registration under section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act; voluntary VAT vendor registration; and specific Income Tax Act elections such as the section 11D research and development allowance election. Hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory statutory rules designed to deny cross-border mismatch outcomes and cannot be elected out of.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration for any vendor whose taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period. Voluntary registration is available where taxable supplies exceed R50,000 in a 12-month period. A non-resident supplier of electronic services to South African residents has a VAT nexus and must register once the total value of such electronic services exceeds R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control for invoices. Vendors must issue valid full or abridged VAT tax invoices within 21 days under section 20 of the VAT Act and must retain electronic records under the Tax Administration Act. SARS has been progressively piloting e-invoicing, but mandatory real-time e-invoicing clearance is not yet in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies to goods physically removed from South Africa where export is completed within the statutory period and SARS receives the required export declaration. For offshore software, cloud and SaaS services supplied to a non-resident customer, zero-rating is available under section 11(2)(l) of the VAT Act where the services are supplied to a non-resident, the services are consumed outside South Africa, payment is received in foreign currency, and the services are not directly connected to South African immovable property, movable property in South Africa, or enjoyed by a South African resident. The supplier must retain contemporaneous evidence of the customer's non-resident status, including registered address, foreign VAT IDs, IP geolocation, and foreign banking or billing details.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) or electronic customs declaration evidencing physical export from South Africa, where goods are involved
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or transport document evidencing physical removal of goods from South Africa
Commercial invoice and underlying export supply contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange bank statement demonstrating receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
For pure SaaS offshore exports: service agreement, invoice, payment records, and evidence of customer non-resident status in lieu of a customs declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow zero-rating where the export or non-resident supply documentation is incomplete or fraudulent, and may retrospectively assess the uncollected output VAT at 15% plus interest. Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, understatement penalties may be imposed at rates determined by the conduct table, with the highest penalties reserved for intentional tax evasion and fraud. Criminal prosecution, additional penalty tax, and personal liability of directors or representative taxpayers may follow in serious cases. Statutory prescription periods may also be extended or removed where a false statement or fraud has been committed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv); day-to-day exchange control administration is delegated to commercial banks licensed as Authorised Dealers under the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 (as amended) and the Currency and Exchanges Manual (CEM).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The rand is fully convertible on the current account without prior SARB approval; capital account movements are subject to administrative documentary controls rather than quantitative ceilings. Non-residents may subscribe for Pty Ltd shares without exchange-control approval, but all inward subscriptions must be reported through an Authorised Dealer under South Africa's Balance-of-Payments (BOP) reporting framework. Current-account repatriations (dividends, royalties, software licence fees) are freely permitted once the SARB requirements on source of funds, tax compliance (SARS Tax Compliance Status) and external loan/non-resident share register declarations are met. Practical hurdles are documentary: BOP classification, inward/outward investment declarations, non-resident share registers, and the strict substance review of prohibited 'loop-structure' arrangements that attempt to externalise ZAR-denominated value.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exchange Control Regulation 7(4), read with the FinSurv Currency and Exchanges Manual: proceeds from the export of goods or services, including SaaS subscription fees and PropTech platform licence services rendered by the Pty Ltd to non-resident counterparties, must be received into South Africa within 180 calendar days of the date of export/performance. Since the August 2016 liberalisation, the mandatory conversion ratio is 0% — an exporter may retain 100% of export receipts in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with a licensed Authorised Dealer, or convert any portion into ZAR at the ruling market rate; no cash surrender quota applies. The operative obligation is repatriation into the SA banking system by deposit into an FCA, not physical conversion to ZAR. Every receipt must be matched to the underlying export invoice in the bank's BOP exchange-control reporting and may be re-deployed only for approved expenditures or conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited (Standard Bank Group)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — inward-investment ZAR current account with parallel USD/EUR FCA treasury module

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited, trading as First National Bank (FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — business current account with integrated FNB FCA and FX online platform
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — corporate current account plus designated Foreign Currency Account (FCA)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — business account with Nedbank Foreign Exchange desk and FCA
Operational Account — premium corporate treasury current account and FCA overlay, well-suited to PropTech treasury structuring

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail and legally impermissible as the sole receipts account. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Mercury, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not Authorised Dealers under the Exchange Control Regulations and cannot satisfy the FCA repatriation requirement; retaining SaaS export receipts in an unlicensed offshore EMI account beyond the 180-day repatriation window is an exchange-control breach absent a SARB departure approval or external-account authorisation. EMIs may function only as a voluntary collection gateway when swept daily (T+0/T+1) into a licensed SA Authorised-Dealer FCA, with each sweep BOP-tagged and the foreign account formally declared. Any long-term treasury balance held on an EMI ledger is a high-risk compliance event; the documented FinSurv framework requires the Pty Ltd's transactional liquidity to reside within the South African banking system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance by at least one director or authorised signatory is effectively mandated for the initial onboarding interview at Tier 1 SA banks; fully remote opening for a non-resident-owned (Pty) Ltd is not a standard offering. Where the entire executive layer is non-resident, banks ordinarily require the international/corporate onboarding desk to conduct a video-identity KYC session followed by a physical visit of the authorised signatory to Johannesburg or Cape Town (or a bank relationship manager visit to the director's domicile with notarised wet-ink execution). Identity verification follows section 21 of the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA): certified and apostilled/legalised passport, residential address proof, CIPC company extract, Memorandum of Incorporation, beneficial-ownership schedule covering all natural persons with 25% or more of the shareholding, SARS tax clearances, and a signed Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner or director with unverifiable source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled/legalised passport and birth certificate; notarised source-of-wealth statement quantifying net worth; audited or reviewed financial statements of the owning entity for 3 years; home-jurisdiction bank reference with transaction history; tax-residency certificate under the applicable double-taxation agreement; SARS Tax Compliance Status; sworn explanation of each material wealth-creation event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity low-value SaaS subscription inflows flagged as structuring or unexplained turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PropTech-specific AML/CFT risk assessment and written compliance manual; transaction-monitoring dashboard evidencing account-balance velocity rules; matched SaaS invoices, platform rate cards and merchant settlement ledgers (Stripe Billing, ACH Direct); tenant-level and landlord-level CDD/EDD files; independent registered auditor's letter reconciling platform turnover to bank receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hits against real-estate counterparties (tenant and landlord registries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated screening logs against SA FIC, OFAC, UN and EU consolidated sanctions lists; negative-news research rationale; enhanced due diligence questionnaire completed by the bank; board resolution authorising continued activity after EDD; documentary proof that counterparties are not designated persons and that no funds flow from or through high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque intermediate ownership (tax-transparent LLC or LLP injecting equity)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain-of-ownership diagram to each ultimate individual; apostilled constitutive documents (LLC agreement, partnership deed); FICA section 21B beneficial-ownership register; legal opinions from counsel in both jurisdictions confirming that funding is not proceeds of crime; bank references, audited accounts and source-of-funds statements for each intermediate layer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 into the Pty Ltd's ZAR current account or dedicated FCA at an Authorised Dealer; payment instructions must state the BOP purpose code for direct investment — equity subscription — and reference the board resolution approving the share allotment under section 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. The Authorised Dealer records the inward investment through the South African BOP reporting system (inward investment declaration) and the company updates its non-resident share register. Compliance protocol: (1) deliver to the bank the share subscription agreement, Memorandum of Incorporation and director resolution for issuance before receipt of funds; (2) at receipt secure the dealer's FX transaction slip with BOP classification and verification that the remitter is the named non-resident shareholder; (3) apply funds promptly to issued share capital. Any shareholder loan injection must instead be registered under the external-loan rules with the loan approval letter raised before disbursement; subsequent divestment remittances require proof that equity was originally imported through Authorised-Dealer rails.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 remains the primary clearing rail for all cross-border trade disbursements of a PropTech SaaS treasury: subscription licence fees to cloud providers, commissions paid to non-resident sales affiliates, software royalties, intercompany service fees and dividend distributions. Dividend and interest remittances require, in addition to the SWIFT instruction: SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) verified by the bank, audited annual financial statements, a solvency and liquidity board resolution under section 4 of the Companies Act, dividends tax withheld at 20% (treaty-reduced where a DTA applies) and non-resident registration evidence in the share register. For physical hardware imports used in the property-management arm (IoT access devices, CCTV, smart-lock readers), Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710) and documentary collections (SWIFT MT400) are available through the Authorised Dealer, with the import declaration and 180-day settlement currency rules applied. Same-day domestic settlement is executed via SAMOS/EFT, while cross-border transfers use SWIFT gpi with UETR tracking to evidence the purpose code at the receiving bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla forward exchange contracts (FECs) entered into with a South African Authorised Dealer, covering firm SaaS export receipts and payables with documented underlying commercial exposure
Outright USD/EUR/GBP buy-or-sell FECs for export proceeds within the 180-day surrender and FCA retention window

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore as a hedging overlay (never speculative) where the onshore FEC market is illiquid for the specific ZAR cross, subject to FinSurv evidence of the real-economy exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS/CCS) permitted in respect of the Pty Ltd's external loan liabilities or long-term shareholder funding facilities registered with the Authorised Dealer

Vanilla foreign-exchange options (premium-payable) used as risk overlay on the subscription collection and disbursement pipelines, at all times matched to a documented commercial exposure in the FX risk management policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty ZAR 450 (approx USD 25) for arrears up to 12 months, escalating linearly to a maximum ZAR 2,700 for arrears exceeding 60 months; continued non-compliance triggers CIPC final warning and administrative strike-off (deregistration) under section 82(3) of the Companies Act, followed by asset vesting in the State and loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) preparation (not filed with CIPC for private companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and shareholders (retained in company records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the company's financial year (Companies Act s30(4))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors personally liable for failure to prepare AFS; CIPC may issue a compliance notice and ultimately refer the matter for civil or criminal sanction under section 30 read with section 75.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (or date specified in SARS notice of assessment filing obligation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS administrative penalty imposed for each month of non-filing based on taxable income (Tax Administration Act s210); SARS may issue a default assessment and add statutory interest; prolonged non-compliance can trigger criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First provisional payment due within 6 months from the start of the financial year; second payment due on or before the last business day of the financial year; optional 'top-up' payment due within 6 months after financial year-end for year-ends other than December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS understatement penalty (20% to 100% of tax underpaid) plus interest at prescribed rate on late payment (s89 Tax Administration Act); willful non-submission may result in criminal sanction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private company must have its annual financial statements independently audited if its Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more (Companies Act s30(2)(b) read with Regulation 28). If PIS is between 100 and 349, an independent review is required unless the company is owner-managed and qualifies for a CIPC disclosure exemption. If PIS is below 100, the company is exempt from mandatory audit and review provided its AFS are prepared by or under the supervision of a director.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) as issued by the IASB, or IFRS for SMEs as adopted in South Africa. Private companies without public accountability may elect IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC Annual Return includes a mandatory Beneficial Ownership Declaration. The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register under section 56B of the Companies Act and confirm the UBO details with CIPC annually as part of the annual return. Any change to beneficial ownership during the year must be recorded in the register and filed with CIPC within 30 days of the change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% prior years)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Corporation ('SBC') graduated rates for companies with gross income below ZAR 20 million: 0% on first ZAR 95,750; 7% on next bracket; 21% on next bracket; 27% above ZAR 320,000 (2025 scale). Section 11D R&D incentive: 150% super-deduction for qualifying R&D (pre-2024); from 1 January 2024 restructured to full deduction plus 10% R&D tax credit. Section 12B accelerated first-year allowance for renewable energy (100%-125%). Section 12C/12E accelerated capital allowances for manufacturing plant and machinery (SBCs: 100% write-off). No specific PropTech patent box.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carry-forward of assessed losses under s.20(1) Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, restricted to taxable income derived from trade; forfeited on change-in-shareholding plus change-in-trade under s.20A; no carry-back.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Corporate Income Tax return) filed exclusively via SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za); annual return submitted by the company or tax practitioner; provisional tax returns (IRP6) filed via eFiling at months 6 and 12 of the year of assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (ITR14). Provisional tax (IRP6): two compulsory estimates per tax year plus a voluntary third top-up return within six months after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 due within 12 months of the end of the year of assessment (SARS may impose earlier due dates via corporate filing-season notices). Provisional payments: first installment on or before the last day of month 6 of the year of assessment; second on or before the last day of the year of assessment; third top-up within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, registration/company number, SARS tax reference number, public officer identity, financial year-end, industry code (ISIC 6201), contact details and banking details for refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A South African incorporated (Pty) Ltd is tax-resident in South Africa and files on worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders are not disclosed; the company must appoint a resident public officer (s.246 TAA) responsible for returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide gross receipts excluding exempt income: SaaS subscription revenue (Stripe Billing/ACH), property management platform fees, tenant screening charges, setup/implementation fees, and interest or incidental revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue income on an accrual basis; translate foreign-currency receipts at the SARS ruling exchange rate for the year of assessment. No special export exemption for SaaS revenue of a resident company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local dividends (s.10(1)(k)), foreign dividends qualifying for the participation exemption (s.10B), and other statutorily exempt receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule detailing exempt foreign dividends and supporting proof of shareholding percentage and underlying tax (s.10B calculations).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenditure incurred in the production of income under s.11(a): salaries, cloud infrastructure, software development, hosting, marketing, professional fees, depreciation, and s.11D R&D deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border intra-group charges (management fees, IP royalties, recharges) must satisfy the arm's-length requirement of s.31 and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of assessed loss carried forward from prior years under s.20, deductible against taxable income derived from trade up to nil.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm continuity of shareholding and trade under s.20A if foreign investors acquired or restructured shareholding during the year; failure to do so forfeits the loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 - Section F: Taxable income and normal tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income (gross income less exemptions, deductions and assessed loss) multiplied by the 27% corporate rate; SBC progressive rates apply if turnover below ZAR 20 million and all shareholders are natural persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special standalone rate for foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd; standard 27% unless SBC eligibility is met (all shareholders natural persons - note: foreign corporate shareholders disqualify SBC status).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 - Section G: Rebates and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits against normal tax: provisional tax payments (IRP6), foreign tax credits under s.6quat, withholding taxes on interest and royalties, and donations/penalty adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax credit schedules and SARS notices confirming provisional credits; any DTA-reduced withholding must be evidenced by the non-resident's TRC on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic declaration by the public officer or authorized director confirming the return is true and complete, and that the estimated figures are based on the financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Knowingly submitting false particulars constitutes a criminal offence under s.234/235 TAA (imprisonment up to 5 years) and triggers an understatement penalty up to 150%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-submission: fixed-amount administrative penalty (s.210 TAA) of ZAR 250 to ZAR 4,000 per month of non-compliance scaled by turnover, capped at 35 months; plus possible percentage penalty of 10% of assessed tax. Understatement penalty (s.222-223 TAA): 10% (standard), 25% (reasonable care not taken), 50% (no reasonable grounds), 75% (impermissible avoidance), 150% (intentional tax evasion). Late payment interest at SARS prescribed rate (SARB repo rate + 7 percentage points) compounded monthly. Criminal: s.235 TAA fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 or imprisonment up to 2 years for failure to submit; s.234 TAA for tax evasion, imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% dividends tax (Dividends Tax Act 31 of 2011, s.64E) on any dividend paid by a South African resident (Pty) Ltd to a non-resident beneficial owner of shares; the company is the withholding agent and must remit the tax to SARS within 30 days of the dividend payment date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty rate, the company must obtain from the non-resident beneficial owner, prior to payment: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate ('TRC') issued by the foreign tax authority; and (ii) a signed declaration confirming treaty residence and beneficial ownership of the dividend (SARS form DTD – Declaration by Beneficial Owner). The withholding agent retains these documents and files the dividend tax return (DTR02/DTR03) via eFiling, remitting the treaty-reduced amount. If the reduced rate cannot be evidenced at payment, the non-resident must withhold 20% and may apply to SARS for a refund (within 3 years) attaching the TRC, declaration and proof of tax withheld. Common treaty rates: 5% for corporate shareholders holding at least 10% of capital/voting rights; 10%-15% for portfolio and other holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory withholding tax (s.49B Income Tax Act) on payments to non-residents for IP, software licences, know-how and technical services; final tax, reduced to 0%-12% under applicable DTAs (e.g., 0% under the SA-US treaty where royalty is exclusively taxable in residence state). Interest: 15% statutory withholding tax (s.50B) on interest paid by a resident to a non-resident, subject to exemptions for SA government, municipal and listed-bond interest; treaty reduction commonly 0%-10%. Both require the same TRC + declaration protocol and eFiling remittance within 30 days of payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: SARS TP record-keeping rules under s.29 TAA (effective for years of assessment commencing on/after 1 April 2023): Local File required where the aggregate value of covered connected-person transactions exceeds ZAR 5 million in the year; Master File required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds ZAR 10 billion; Country-by-Country Report due where the group exceeds the same ZAR 10 billion threshold. Penalties for non-compliance: administrative penalty and understatement penalty up to 150%.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute; substance is enforced through: (i) s.103(1) Income Tax Act general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) – arrangements lacking commercial substance and aimed at tax avoidance are voided; (ii) s.31 transfer-pricing secondary adjustments (deemed dividend or loan if the primary adjustment is not repatriated); (iii) s.9D controlled-foreign-company rules requiring a 'foreign business establishment' (real premises, employees, local management) before foreign passive income escapes attribution; (iv) the OECD Multilateral Instrument – Principal Purpose Test (PPT) denying treaty benefits where obtaining the treaty benefit is a principal purpose; and (v) the common-law substance-over-form and sham doctrines. A (Pty) Ltd operating a PropTech platform must maintain real board decisions, local employees, SA cloud/data operations, and genuine R&D in South Africa; offshore management fees or IP royalty stripping without local substance will be re-characterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to register for CIT, intentional omission of SaaS subscription revenue, false invoices (ghost vendors), fabricated s.11D R&D claims, backdating agreements, or destroying books and records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 150% of the shortfall (s.223 TAA) plus interest at repo rate + 7%; criminal conviction under s.234 TAA: fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; SARS may also make additional assessments for 3 to 6 years (s.99 TAA; 6 years where fraudulent).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate attract criminal liability as co-perpetrators; representative-taxpayer liability under s.159/160 TAA for unpaid corporate tax where the default is attributable to the director's fraud, negligence or default; civil claims by SARS for the shortfall; travel bans via court interdict in pending prosecutions; disqualification as directors under the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length management fees to foreign parent, excessive software licensing or royalty charges to offshore group companies, interest-free or low-interest shareholder loans, artificial allocation of SaaS profits to a low-tax offshore entity while functions/risks remain in South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment increasing taxable income under s.31; secondary adjustment deeming the excess a dividend or loan to the connected person (triggering 20% dividends tax); understatement penalty of 50%-150% for 'substantial understatement' or 'intentional tax evasion'; interest; possible CFC-attribution adjustments under s.9D.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving sham transfer-pricing structures may be assessed as 'relevant persons' participating in an impermissible avoidance arrangement (s.103); personal liability for the company's tax debt under s.160 TAA; restitution claims by shareholders/creditors under s.77 Companies Act; criminal referral for tax evasion with imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Insufficient Economic Substance (GAAR and Treaty Abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SA entity with registered office at a virtual mail service, no employees, no board minutes, no local operational control, all SaaS platform functions and data hosted/managed by foreign parent, dividends paid to a treaty-holding structure inserted solely to access a low DTA rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the shell arrangement under s.103(1) GAAR and tax the substance-owner directly; denial of treaty benefits under the MLI Principal Purpose Test; deemed dividends on secondary adjustments; 75% understatement penalty for impermissible avoidance; re-characterization of payments as taxable distributions; criminal prosecution for assisting in tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face personal exposure for restitution of corporate assets diverted abroad; courts may lift the corporate veil where the company is a mere façade (common-law veil piercing); travel restrictions and contempt proceedings for failing to produce records; imprisonment up to 5 years for aiding a tax-evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Remittance Taxes (Dividends, Royalties, Interest)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding 20% dividends tax; paying foreign royalties or interest without 15% WHT or treaty documentation; failing to file the DTR return or remit the withheld amounts within 30 days; making deemed-dividend distributions via the secondary adjustment without settling dividends tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company as withholding agent is personally liable for the un-withheld tax (s.38 TAA); additional understatement penalty of up to 150% of the un-withheld amount; interest at repo rate + 7%; criminal fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years for failure to withhold (s.236).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are joint and severally liable for unremitted withholding taxes under s.160 TAA, collectible by SARS by civil execution against personal assets; SARS can prevent foreign travel and financial transfers where amounts are in dispute; criminal conviction of responsible officers on the basis of personal participation or negligent oversight.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PropTech platform as an unlicensed payment intermediary handling tenant deposits, rental collection, escrow balances, or property proceeds without registering under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) as an accountable institution; accepting cash above statutory thresholds; failure to conduct client due diligence or report suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA administrative penalties up to ZAR 10 million per non-compliance plus daily penalties; the Conduct of Financial Institutions ('COFI') and Damages: supervisory referrals; funds may be frozen by the Financial Intelligence Centre; SARS will treat unexplained deposits as gross income with a 150% understatement penalty; criminal referral for money laundering (POCA) carries fines and imprisonment up to 15 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly involved in laundering proceeds or circumventing FICA duties face predicate-offence liability, conviction-based confiscation of assets, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 15 years; civil liability to the Financial Intelligence Centre for penalty amounts where the non-compliance resulted from willful blindness; disqualification from serving as directors.
